title: 424. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Simplifying Trigonometric Expressions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Rewrite a product of sine and secant as a single function.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\sin\theta\sec\theta\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Replace \(\sec\theta\) by \(\frac{1}{\cos\theta}\): \(\sin\theta\cdot\frac{1}{\cos\theta}=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\tan\theta\). The cotangent would have the cosine in the numerator.
questions.hint: Write the secant in terms of cosine.

questions.concept: Simplifying a quotient with a Pythagorean numerator
questions.learningObjective: Simplify a quotient after replacing an expression by a square.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\frac{1-\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Since \(1-\sin^2\theta=\cos^2\theta\), the quotient is \(\frac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta}=\cos\theta\). One factor of cosine cancels; the result is not the reciprocal \(\sec\theta\).
questions.hint: Replace the numerator using the Pythagorean identity, then cancel.

questions.concept: Combining terms over a common denominator
questions.learningObjective: Simplify a sum by writing tangent as a quotient and combining terms.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\cos\theta+\sin\theta\tan\theta\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Write \(\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\): \(\cos\theta+\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}=\frac{\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}=\frac{1}{\cos\theta}=\sec\theta\). The numerator becomes \(1\), but the denominator \(\cos\theta\) remains.
questions.hint: Put both terms over the denominator \(\cos\theta\) and simplify the numerator.

questions.concept: Factoring a difference of fourth powers
questions.learningObjective: Simplify a difference of fourth powers by factoring as a difference of squares.
questions.question: For every angle \(\theta\), \(\sin^4\theta-\cos^4\theta\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Factor as a difference of squares: \(\sin^4\theta-\cos^4\theta=(\sin^2\theta-\cos^2\theta)(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)=(\sin^2\theta-\cos^2\theta)\cdot 1\). A difference of fourth powers is not the fourth power of a difference; at \(\theta=0\) the original expression is \(-1\), while \((0-1)^4=1\).
questions.hint: Treat the expression as \(a^2-b^2\) with \(a=\sin^2\theta\) and \(b=\cos^2\theta\).

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a difference of a function and its reciprocal.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\sec\theta-\cos\theta\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Combine over \(\cos\theta\): \(\frac{1}{\cos\theta}-\cos\theta=\frac{1-\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta}=\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta}=\sin\theta\cdot\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\sin\theta\tan\theta\). The expression \(\sin\theta\cot\theta\) equals \(\cos\theta\), which is different.
questions.hint: Write the secant as a fraction and subtract using a common denominator.

questions.concept: Product involving one plus tangent squared
questions.learningObjective: Simplify a product using the tangent-secant identity.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\left(1+\tan^2\theta\right)\cos^2\theta\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Since \(1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta=\frac{1}{\cos^2\theta}\), the product is \(\frac{1}{\cos^2\theta}\cdot\cos^2\theta=1\). Distributing gives the same result, \(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1\); forgetting to multiply the first term by \(\cos^2\theta\) leads to the incorrect \(1+\sin^2\theta\).
questions.hint: Replace \(1+\tan^2\theta\) by a single squared function, or distribute carefully.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a difference of cosecant and sine to a product.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\csc\theta-\sin\theta\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Combine over \(\sin\theta\): \(\frac{1}{\sin\theta}-\sin\theta=\frac{1-\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta}=\frac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta}=\cos\theta\cdot\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}=\cos\theta\cot\theta\). The expression \(\cos\theta\tan\theta\) equals \(\sin\theta\), which is different.
questions.hint: Write the cosecant as a fraction, subtract, and apply the Pythagorean identity to the numerator.

questions.learningObjective: Simplify a product of a quotient function and a reciprocal function.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\cot\theta\sec\theta\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Rewrite with sine and cosine: \(\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\cdot\frac{1}{\cos\theta}=\frac{1}{\sin\theta}=\csc\theta\). The cosine cancels, leaving the reciprocal of the sine.
questions.hint: Convert both functions to sine and cosine and cancel the common factor.

questions.concept: Simplifying a difference with unlike denominators
questions.learningObjective: Combine a rational trigonometric expression with a tangent and simplify.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\frac{\cos\theta}{1-\sin\theta}-\tan\theta\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Use the common denominator \(\cos\theta(1-\sin\theta)\): the numerator is \(\cos^2\theta-\sin\theta(1-\sin\theta)=\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta-\sin\theta=1-\sin\theta\). The factor \(1-\sin\theta\) cancels, leaving \(\frac{1}{\cos\theta}=\sec\theta\).
questions.hint: Write \(\tan\theta\) as \(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\) and combine the two fractions over a common denominator.

questions.concept: Simplifying a sum of reciprocal fractions
questions.learningObjective: Add two rational trigonometric expressions and simplify the result.
questions.question: Wherever it is defined, \(\frac{\sin\theta}{1+\cos\theta}+\frac{1+\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\) simplifies to which expression?
questions.explanation: Over the common denominator \(\sin\theta(1+\cos\theta)\), the numerator is \(\sin^2\theta+(1+\cos\theta)^2=\sin^2\theta+1+2\cos\theta+\cos^2\theta=2+2\cos\theta=2(1+\cos\theta)\). Cancelling \(1+\cos\theta\) leaves \(\frac{2}{\sin\theta}=2\csc\theta\).
questions.hint: Add the fractions, expand the square, and use the Pythagorean identity in the numerator.
